sentence: This project develops three-dimensional shell arrays of electrodes and fluids that surround brain organoids to stimulate and measure their electrical and biochemical microenvironment.
This project develops engineered T cells that target acute myeloid leukemia and tests whether they persist longer and cause less toxicity in mouse models.
This project makes mouse strains with altered genes to study how certain proteins control immune functions in dendritic cells and T cells.
This project studies how protein misfolding changes neuronal gene expression in multiple system atrophy, to look for biomarker candidates of the disease.
This project builds models that link measurements from individual brain cell types to how neural circuits work in the human neocortex.
This project uses a CRISPR technology and sequencing to make hundreds of zebrafish models of human disease and measure the molecular changes in each.
This project studies how one gene controls the function and development of regulatory T cells, to make these cells from human pluripotent stem cells.
This project tries to find out how lower estradiol after menopause changes sarcomeric proteins and slows relaxation in aged female hearts.
This project provides statistical and computational support for laboratory experiments and clinical trials on targeting replication stress in endometrial cancer.
This project builds statistical methods using machine learning to study how air pollution over time affects chronic lung disease.
This project provides small animal imaging tools, including positron emission tomography and computed tomography, for cancer research.
This project studies how one protein helps the intestine absorb dietary lipids and how this affects metabolic health.
This project holds a conference on how sleep interacts with functions of the brain and body.
This project tries to find out how defects in protein synthesis and degradation drive lymphatic and venous malformations and whether targeting them can help treatment.
This project analyzes data from mass spectrometry, genome editing and cryo-electron microscopy to work out structures of HIV and human protein complexes.
This project develops drugs that block one protein to slow the growth and invasion of glioblastoma tumors.
This project studies how cancers misuse normal developmental and stem cell signals to grow, spread and evade therapy.
This project studies the structure and workings of calcium channels called inositol trisphosphate receptors and how disease disrupts them.
